A daily React user says Next.js is the only framework where half the time they can't tell what its error messages mean, if they get any. They report losing countless hours to weird hydration issues.
A developer with 20+ years in Perl/PHP/Java/Python says Next.js and React gave them back the joy of frontend development. They acknowledge many gotchas, especially when not hosting on Vercel.

Criticism of the App Router: compared with mature Express-style APIs, the middleware API is called abysmal. The commenter also dislikes replacing a request parameter with global functions like cookies() and headers().

Next.js stacks browser, middleware, edge vs. node, and SSR layers, which causes confusion about where code runs. One commenter says it only fits global B2C apps willing to pay Vercel with no background jobs. Otherwise they recommend a React+Vite SPA or Rails SSR.

A developer who has tried many stacks says their large Next.js app was painful from start to finish: 'weird, slow, cumbersome or completely insane.' It is the only thing they still maintain that they hate.
Despite disliking most things about Next.js, one team finds Claude Code noticeably better at Next.js than at other frameworks.

One user expected to hate the App Router because of HN sentiment, but after three production-scale projects calls it a great isomorphic TS framework, the closest thing in JS to Rails/Phoenix 'batteries included.'

A team removed Next.js after its patching of the fetch prototype cost them days of debugging why file uploads above ~100KB failed. They feel Next does too much, moves too fast, and reinvents the wheel every few months.
One developer says Nuxt is miles ahead in DX: in Next.js the architecture stands in your way, while in Nuxt everything just works.
One commenter argues that running backend code in Next.js is incoherent even for an MVP. They say many issues are features that only work on, and lock you into, the Vercel platform.

On the CVSS 10.0 RCE in React Server Components affecting Next.js, a commenter says Next.js/RSC 'has become the new PHP' and expects bots to start scanning for '/_next' paths the way they scan for '/wp-content'.
One user says Next is only good for its static build output and they'll leave if that support is dropped. Another notes that static builds 'save the day' against the RCE.
A team that built an MVP with Next.js found it a pleasure to work with. They cited no tooling setup, SSR plus SPA rendering out of the box, filesystem routing, and automatic per-route code splitting.
The same MVP team hit problems: importing non-JS files like normalize.css from node_modules, missing page transition animations, server/client inconsistencies, and scroll restoration on routing.
A developer rebuilt emailprivacytester.com in Next.js v1 and found it a pleasure. Because v1 couldn't add custom API routes, they had to split it into a Next frontend and a separate Express backend.
Criticism of Next's component-scoped CSS (styled-jsx): one user's large project had duplicated CSS in every component. Another says styled-jsx's encapsulation makes external overrides hard.
At launch, one user was impressed that middle-click/ctrl-click worked flawlessly, but noticed forward/back navigation only worked one level deep.

One user loves Next but says the Next team builds features for 0.1% of users while ignoring long-standing community requests for better performance. They welcome Cloudflare's Vite-based reimplementation.

A team migrated from OpenNext on Cloudflare to React Router 7 because deploying Next.js outside Vercel was hard. Others say Next makes everything hard except deploying to Vercel, which feels like vendor lock-in.
A commenter disputes that Next.js is well-specified. They say it has many undocumented or poorly documented behaviors that have repeatedly caused frustration, despite its extensive docs.
